001.Black_footed_Albatross.habitat: Open ocean, particularly near the North Pacific Ocean and the Hawaiian Islands.
001.Black_footed_Albatross.range_description: Breeds exclusively on the Hawaiian Islands, primarily on the island of Nihoa, and ranges widely across the North Pacific Ocean.
001.Black_footed_Albatross.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its breeding range year-round.
field_marks: Large, dark, sooty-black body with a pale gray head and neck.
Distinctive black feet and a white band across the wings.
Long, narrow wings and a deeply forked tail.
Black bill with a pale tip.
001.Black_footed_Albatross.diet: Primarily consumes squid and fish, often foraging far out at sea.

similar_species.name: Laysan Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Smaller in size, with a more white head and a less pronounced black band across the wings.

similar_species.name: Waved Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Larger and has a more rounded head and a distinctive white patch on the neck, not found in Black-footed Albatross.

001.Black_footed_Albatross.fun_fact: Black-footed Albatrosses are known for their long-distance foraging trips, often traveling thousands of kilometers from their breeding colonies.

002.Laysan_Albatross.habitat: Open ocean, particularly around the Laysan Atoll and other tropical Pacific islands.
002.Laysan_Albatross.range_description: Endemic to the central Pacific Ocean, primarily found around the Laysan Atoll, Midway Atoll, and other nearby islands.
002.Laysan_Albatross.migration: Non-migratory; remains within its breeding range year-round.
field_marks: White plumage with a dark gray mantle and a black bill.
Dark eyes with a pale ring around the eye.
Long, narrow wings with a distinctive white trailing edge.
Short, square tail with a dark tip.
002.Laysan_Albatross.diet: Primarily consumes squid and small fish, foraging over open ocean.

similar_species.name: Black-footed Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Black-footed Albatross has a longer, more pointed bill and a darker underwing compared to the Laysan Albatross.

similar_species.name: Wedge-tailed Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Wedge-tailed Albat,ross has a much longer, more wedge-shaped tail and a more robust bill.

002.Laysan_Albatross.fun_fact: Laysan Albatrosses are known for their long-distance flights and strong pair bonds, often returning to the same nest site year after year.

003.Sooty_Albatross.habitat: Open ocean, particularly near the Antarctic and sub-Antarctic regions.
003.Sooty_Albatross.range_description: Breeds on the South Georgia Islands and the South Sandwich Islands, and is found in the Southern Ocean during the non-breeding season.
003.Sooty_Albatross.migration: Non-migratory; remains in the Southern Ocean year-round.
field_marks: Dark sooty-gray plumage with a white underbelly.
Broad, dark eye stripe that extends from the base of the bill to the nape.
Short, stubby bill with a dark tip.
Long, narrow wings with a distinctive white edge.
Dark legs and feet.
003.Sooty_Albatross.diet: Primarily feeds on squid and krill, occasionally consuming small fish.

similar_species.name: Black-browed Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Black-browed Albatross has a more contrasting black eye stripe and a paler underbelly compared to the sooty-gray coloration of the Sooty Albatross.

similar_species.name: Light-mantled Albatross
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Light-mantled Albatross has a lighter, more uniform mantle and a more distinct white underbelly, whereas the Sooty Albatross has a sooty-gray mantle.

003.Sooty_Albatross.fun_fact: Sooty Albatrosses are known for their long-distance foraging trips, often traveling thousands of kilometers from their breeding colonies to feed.

004.Groove_billed_Ani.habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests, often near water sources.
004.Groove_billed_Ani.range_description: Found in eastern South America, including Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina.
field_marks: Dark, glossy black plumage with a distinctive white stripe running along the center of the breast.
Short, stout bill with a deep groove on the upper mandible.
White eye ring and dark eye stripe.
Long, slender tail with a slight upward curve.
004.Groove_billed_Ani.diet: Insectivorous, primarily consuming beetles, crickets, and other small invertebrates.

similar_species.name: Smooth-billed Ani
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Lacks the white stripe on the breast and has a smoother, less grooved bill.

similar_species.name: Crested Ani
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Has a prominent crest on the head, whereas the Groove-billed Ani lacks this feature.

004.Groove_billed_Ani.fun_fact: The Groove-billed Ani is known for its unique, loud, and often raucous call, which is used to defend territory and attract mates.

005.Crested_Auklet.habitat: Coastal marine environments, particularly rocky shores and islands in the North Pacific Ocean.
005.Crested_Auklet.range_description: Breeds in the Aleutian Islands and surrounding areas of Alaska, and winters along the coasts of California, Oregon, and Washington.
005.Crested_Auklet.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its breeding and wintering range year-round.
field_marks: Black head with a prominent white stripe running from the base of the bill to the nape.
White underparts with a dark brown back and wings.
Short, stout bill with a slight downward curve.
Dark eyes with a pale ring around the iris.
005.Crested_Auklet.diet: Primarily feeds on small fish and plankton, foraging in shallow coastal waters.

similar_species.name: Least Auklet
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Lacks the distinct white stripe on the head; has a more uniform dark head and a paler underparts.

similar_species.name: Rhinoceros Auklet
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Larger in size with a more pronounced black-and-white facial pattern and a distinctive horn-like structure on the bill.

005.Crested_Auklet.fun_fact: Crested Auklets are known for their unique breeding behavior, where the male performs a courtship display by puffing up its head and neck to appear larger.

006.Least_Auklet.habitat: Coastal waters and rocky shores of the North Pacific Ocean, particularly in Alaska and British Columbia.
006.Least_Auklet.range_description: Breeds in colonies on rocky islands and coastal cliffs from Alaska to northern California, and winters along the coasts of Japan and the Bering Sea.
006.Least_Auklet.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its breeding range year-round.
field_marks: Small, compact seabird with a dark, glossy black body.
White underparts, including a white belly and undertail coverts.
Short, stout bill with a slight downward curve.
Dark eyes with a pale ring around the iris.
Short, square-ended tail with a small white tip.
006.Least_Auklet.diet: Primarily consumes small fish, plankton, and krill, foraged near the surface in coastal waters.

similar_species.name: Least Tern
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Least Auklet is much smaller and has a dark body with white underparts, while Least Tern is larger with a white forehead and a black cap.

similar_species.name: Common Murre
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Common Murre is larger with a more elongated body and a distinct black-and-white plumage pattern, whereas Least Auklet is more compact and uniformly dark with white underparts.

006.Least_Auklet.fun_fact: Least Auklets are known for their high-pitched, staccato calls and their ability to dive and resurface quickly to catch prey.

007.Parakeet_Auklet.habitat: Coastal marine environments, particularly rocky shores and islands in the North Pacific Ocean.
007.Parakeet_Auklet.range_description: Breeds in the Aleutian Islands and the Pribilof Islands, Alaska, and winters along the coasts of British Columbia, Alaska, and northern California.
007.Parakeet_Auklet.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its breeding range year-round.
field_marks: Small, compact seabird with a distinctive parrot-like bill that is black with a yellow tip.
White underparts with a dark gray back and wings.
Black eyes with a pale eye ring.
Short, square tail with a dark tip.
007.Parakeet_Auklet.diet: Primarily consumes small fish, plankton, and krill, foraged near the surface of the ocean.

similar_species.name: Least Auklet
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: The Least Auklet has a more rounded head and a shorter, more conical bill compared to the Parakeet Auklet. It also has a more extensive white area on the underparts.

similar_species.name: Razorbill
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: The Razorbill has a longer, more pointed bill and lacks the distinct eye ring found in the Parakeet Auklet. It also has a more contrasting black-and-white plumage pattern.

007.Parakeet_Auklet.fun_fact: Parakeet Auklets are known for their loud, raucous calls, which are often heard during breeding colonies.

008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.habitat: Coastal marine environments, including rocky shores and islands, often near kelp forests.
008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.range_description: Breeds in the northern Pacific Ocean, from Alaska to Japan, and winters along the coasts of California, Oregon, and Washington.
008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.migration: Non-migratory; breeds in summer and remains in coastal areas year-round.
field_marks: Black head with a white stripe running from the base of the bill to the eye.
White underparts with a dark back and wings.
Short, thick bill with a prominent black tip.
Dark eyes with a white ring around the eye.
008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.diet: Primarily fish, especially small schooling fish like sand lance and herring, also consumes crustaceans.

similar_species.name: Least Auklet
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Smaller in size, with a more contrasting black and white plumage, and a shorter, more pointed bill.

similar_species.name: Parakeet Auklet
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Has a more distinct white eye ring and a paler underparts, with a more elongated bill.

008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.fun_fact: Rhinoceros Auklets are known for their distinctive 'bouncing' behavior on rocky shores, where they leap from one rock to another while foraging.

009.Brewer_Blackbird.habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural fields, and shrubby areas, often near water sources.
009.Brewer_Blackbird.range_description: Breeds in the western United States, from southern California to western Texas, and southern Arizona. Winters in Mexico and Central America.
009.Brewer_Blackbird.migration: Non-migratory; some populations may move short distances during harsh weather.
field_marks: Black plumage with a distinctive yellow eye stripe.
Dark bill with a yellow base.
White undertail coverts visible during flight.
Short, square tail with a slight blackish tip.
009.Brewer_Blackbird.diet: Insectivorous, but also consumes seeds, fruits, and small vertebrates.

similar_species.name: Rusty Blackbird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Rusty Blackbird has a more uniformly dark plumage with a rusty tinge, and lacks the yellow eye stripe of the Brewer Blackbird.

similar_species.name: Red-winged Blackbird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Red-winged Blackbird has a red and yellow epaulet on the wings, and is typically smaller with a shorter tail.

009.Brewer_Blackbird.fun_fact: Brewer Blackbirds are known for their loud, complex songs, especially during the breeding season.

010.Red_winged_Blackbird.habitat: Freshwater marshes, wetlands, and adjacent grassy areas, especially in the eastern and central United States.
010.Red_winged_Blackbird.range_description: Breeds across eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida, and western North America from central Canada to California. Winters in the southern United States and Mexico.
010.Red_winged_Blackbird.migration: Migratory; breeds in summer and winters in warmer regions.
field_marks: Male has a striking black body with bright red and yellow epaulets on the wings.
Female is brown with faint streaking and a pale eye ring.
Bill is conical and medium-sized, adapted for catching insects.
Tail is long and slightly forked.
010.Red_winged_Blackbird.diet: Primarily insectivorous, but also consumes seeds, fruits, and small invertebrates.

similar_species.name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Male Yellow-headed Blackbird has a yellow head instead of red epaulets, and a black body with a yellow head.

similar_species.name: Bobolink
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Bobolink is a streaked brown bird with a black head and white belly, and lacks the red epaulets of the Red-winged Blackbird.

010.Red_winged_Blackbird.fun_fact: Red-winged Blackbirds are known for their loud, distinctive 'konk-la-ree' call, often heard during the breeding season.

011.Rusty_Blackbird.habitat: Wetlands, swamps, and riparian forests, often near water.
011.Rusty_Blackbird.range_description: Breeds in boreal forests of Canada and Alaska, and winters along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts of the United States.
011.Rusty_Blackbird.migration: Migratory, traveling long distances between breeding and wintering grounds.
field_marks: Black plumage with a rusty brown wash on the head and neck.
Dark, slender bill with a slight curve.
Short, square tail with a faintly rust-colored edge.
Dark eyes with a pale ring around the iris.
011.Rusty_Blackbird.diet: Insects, seeds, and berries, primarily foraging in wetland vegetation.

similar_species.name: Red-winged Blackbird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Red-winged Blackbird has bright red and yellow shoulder patches, while Rusty Blackbird lacks these and has a more uniformly dark appearance.

similar_species.name: Great Black Hawk
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Great Black Hawk is a larger raptor with a hooked bill and a distinctive black-and-white wing pattern, whereas Rusty Blackbird is a passerine with no such features.

011.Rusty_Blackbird.fun_fact: Rusty Blackbirds are known for their distinctive, low, nasal call and their dramatic population decline in recent decades, though the exact causes remain under study.

012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.habitat: Open wetlands, marshes, and agricultural fields, especially near water.
012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.range_description: Breeds in the central and western United States, from Texas to Montana, and southern Canada. Winters in Mexico and Central America.
012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.migration: Migratory, with some populations remaining in southern regions year-round.
field_marks: Black plumage with a bright yellow head and throat.
Dark eyes and a black bill.
Short, square tail with a slight notch.
White undertail coverts visible during flight.
012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.diet: Primarily seeds, but also insects and berries, especially during breeding season.

similar_species.name: Black-headed Grosbeak
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Larger with a more robust bill, and lacks the yellow head; has a more barred tail.

similar_species.name: Yellow-headed Warbler
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Smaller with a more yellow body, and lacks the black plumage; has a different wing pattern.

012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.fun_fact: Male Yellow-headed Blackbirds are known for their loud, harsh calls, which are often heard during the breeding season.

013.Bobolink.habitat: Open grasslands, marshes, and agricultural fields, especially in the eastern United States.
013.Bobolink.range_description: Breeds in eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida, and winters in South America.
013.Bobolink.migration: Migratory, with populations moving between breeding and wintering grounds across the continent.
field_marks: Adult males have a striking black-and-yellow plumage with a black head, yellow underparts, and a black breast band.
Females are more subdued, with streaked brown plumage and a pale eye ring.
The bill is slender and pointed, adapted for catching insects.
The wings are long and pointed, with a white patch visible in flight.
013.Bobolink.diet: Primarily insectivorous, feeding on grasshoppers, beetles, and other insects, with some seeds in winter.

similar_species.name: Grasshopper Sparrow
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Lacks the black-and-yellow plumage of the Bobolink; has a more brownish coloration and a shorter, more rounded tail.

similar_species.name: Eastern Meadowlark
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: The Eastern Meadowlark has a more yellow belly and a black band across the breast, but lacks the black head and yellow underparts of the Bobolink.

013.Bobolink.fun_fact: The Bobolink is known for its distinctive, bubbly song, which is often heard during the breeding season.

014.Indigo_Bunting.habitat: Open woodlands, thorny shrubs, and brushy habitats across eastern North America.
014.Indigo_Bunting.range_description: Breeds in eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida and western Texas. Migrates to Central America and the Caribbean for winter.
014.Indigo_Bunting.migration: Short-distance migrant, moving to Central America and the Caribbean in winter.
field_marks: Male has brilliant indigo-blue plumage with a black head and white belly.
Female is duller, with gray-brown upperparts and pale underparts.
Bill is slender and conical, adapted for feeding on insects and seeds.
014.Indigo_Bunting.diet: Primarily insectivorous, but also consumes seeds and fruits.

similar_species.name: Blue Jay
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Blue Jay has a more robust body, white markings on the wings and tail, and a blue body with black markings, unlike the Indigo Bunting's uniform blue coloration.

similar_species.name: Eastern Bluebird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Eastern Bluebird has a more rounded body, a blue back, and a rusty-colored breast, whereas the Indigo Bunting has a uniform indigo color and lacks the rusty markings.

014.Indigo_Bunting.fun_fact: The Indigo Bunting is known for its striking coloration, which is more intense in males during the breeding season.

015.Lazuli_Bunting.habitat: Open woodlands, brushy areas, and thorny thickets, often near water sources.
015.Lazuli_Bunting.range_description: Breeds in the western United States and southern Canada, migrating to Mexico and Central America for winter.
015.Lazuli_Bunting.migration: Short-distance migrant, with some populations remaining in warmer regions year-round.
field_marks: Male has a bright blue head and underparts, with a black throat and a white belly.
Female is duller, with a brown head and a streaked breast.
Bill is short and conical, with a dark base and a pale tip.
Wings are dark with two faint white bars, and the tail is square-shaped.
015.Lazuli_Bunting.diet: Primarily seeds, but also insects and berries, especially during the breeding season.

similar_species.name: Indigo Bunting
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Indigo Bunting has a more intense blue coloration on the head and underparts, and lacks the white belly of the Lazuli Bunting.

similar_species.name: Blue Grosbeak
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Blue Grosbeak has a more robust bill and a more extensive blue coloration on the body, with a white belly that is less distinct than in the Lazuli Bunting.

015.Lazuli_Bunting.fun_fact: The Lazuli Bunting is known for its striking blue coloration, which is produced by structural coloration rather than pigments.

016.Painted_Bunting.habitat: Open woodlands, brushy areas, and agricultural fields in the southeastern United States.
016.Painted_Bunting.range_description: Breeds in eastern Texas, Louisiana, and Florida, and winters in southern Mexico and Central America.
016.Painted_Bunting.migration: Irregular migrant; some populations may be non-migratory.
field_marks: Male has brilliant plumage with a bright blue head, red breast, and green back.
Female is duller with a brown head, gray back, and pale underparts.
Bill is short and conical, with a dark tip.
Eyes are dark, and the iris is surrounded by a narrow white ring.
016.Painted_Bunting.diet: Primarily seeds, but also consumes insects and berries.

similar_species.name: Blue Bunting
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Blue Bunting has a more uniform blue coloration with less red and green, and lacks the distinct white eye ring.

similar_species.name: Indigo Bunting
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Indigo Bunting has a more uniform indigo coloration without the red breast or green back of the Painted Bunting.

016.Painted_Bunting.fun_fact: The male Painted Bunting's vibrant plumage is a result of carotenoid pigments obtained from its diet, not genetic factors.

017.Cardinal.habitat: Woodlands, gardens, and shrublands in eastern North America.
017.Cardinal.range_description: Breeds across eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida, and winters in the southern United States.
017.Cardinal.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its breeding range year-round.
field_marks: Male has bright red plumage with a black face and a prominent black mask around the eyes.
Female is more subdued, with a mix of brown, tan, and red feathers.
Both sexes have a distinctive red crown in males and a more muted red crown in females.
Bill is conical and slightly curved, adapted for eating seeds and insects.
017.Cardinal.diet: Primarily seeds, but also eats insects, fruits, and berries.

similar_species.name: Red Cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis)
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: This is the same species; no similar species in the genus Cardinalis.

similar_species.name: Smooth-billed Ani (Ani bimaculata)
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Smooth-billed Ani has a more uniform brown body with a black head and lacks the bright red coloration of the Northern Cardinal.

017.Cardinal.fun_fact: Northern Cardinals are monogamous and often form long-term pair bonds.

018.Spotted_Catbird.habitat: Tropical rainforests of northeastern Australia, particularly in the Wet Tropics region.
018.Spotted_Catbird.range_description: Endemic to the northeastern rainforests of Australia, including the Cape York Peninsula and adjacent islands.
018.Spotted_Catbird.migration: Non-migratory; remains within its tropical rainforest habitat year-round.
field_marks: Black and white plumage with distinctive white spots on the back and flanks.
Dark, rounded head with a white stripe running through the eye.
Short, rounded tail with a white tip.
Black bill with a slight curvature, and a pale pinkish base.
018.Spotted_Catbird.diet: Primarily insectivorous, feeding on insects and other small invertebrates found in the forest understory.

similar_species.name: Gray Catbird
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Gray Catbird (Dumetella carolinensis) is a North American species with a grayish-brown plumage and no distinct white spots.

similar_species.name: Black-tailed Cuscus
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Black-tailed Cuscus (Phalangeris carolae) is a marsupial, not a bird, and has a more arboreal, fluffy appearance.

018.Spotted_Catbird.fun_fact: Spotted Catbirds are known for their loud, cat-like calls, which are used for territorial defense and communication within their dense rainforest habitat.

019.Gray_Catbird.habitat: Brushy thickets, woodland edges, and suburban gardens in eastern North America.
019.Gray_Catbird.range_description: Breeds from southern Canada to northern Florida and western Texas; winters in the southeastern United States.
019.Gray_Catbird.migration: Non-migratory; some populations may move short distances in response to food availability.
field_marks: Dark gray upperparts with a faint, broken white eye stripe.
White underparts with a dark gray breast band.
Short, rounded tail with a dark tip.
Black bill with a slight curve.
019.Gray_Catbird.diet: Insects, berries, and other small fruits.

similar_species.name: Black-throated Blue Warbler
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Black-throated Blue Warbler has a bright blue head and a black throat, while the Gray Catbird has a dark gray head and lacks a distinct throat patch.

similar_species.name: Eastern Towhee
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Eastern Towhee has a rust-colored back and a black face, whereas the Gray Catbird is uniformly dark gray above and white below.

019.Gray_Catbird.fun_fact: The Gray Catbird is known for its mimicry of other birds and environmental sounds, often incorporating cat-like vocalizations into its repertoire.

020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.habitat: Brushy thickets, woodland edges, and overgrown fields in eastern North America.
020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.range_description: Breeds in eastern United States from New England south to Florida and west to Texas. Winters in Central America and the Caribbean.
020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.migration: Non-migratory; remains in breeding range year-round.
field_marks: Bright yellow underparts with a black throat and breast streaking.
Dark brown upperparts with a white eye ring.
Short, conical bill with a slight downward curve.
Long, graduated tail with a white tip.
020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.diet: Insects, berries, and seeds, foraging in dense vegetation.

similar_species.name: Black-billed Cuckoo
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Lacks the yellow underparts; has a more uniform brown plumage with a white eye ring.

similar_species.name: Yellow-throated Warbler
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Smaller with a more restricted yellow throat; lacks the black breast streaking.

020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.fun_fact: The Yellow-breasted Chat is known for its complex, melodious song, which is often described as one of the most intricate in the bird world.

021.Eastern_Towhee.habitat: Brushy fields, overgrown pastures, and woodland edges in open habitats.
021.Eastern_Towhee.range_description: Eastern United States from southern Canada to Florida and Texas.
021.Eastern_Towhee.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its range year-round.
field_marks: Distinctive black head and throat with a white patch on the sides of the face.
White underparts with a black belly.
Dark brown back and wings with faint white streaks.
Short, conical bill.
Black eyes with a white ring around the eye.
021.Eastern_Towhee.diet: Primarily seeds, but also insects and berries, especially during breeding season.

similar_species.name: Spotted Towhee
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Spotted Towhee has a white eye ring and a black-and-white pattern on the face, while the Eastern Towhee has a white patch on the sides of the face and a black throat.

similar_species.name: Horned Lark
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Horned Lark has a more distinct horn-like feather on the crown and a more grayish underparts, whereas the Eastern Towhee has a black throat and white facial patches.

021.Eastern_Towhee.fun_fact: The Eastern Towhee is known for its distinctive 'drink, drink, drink' call and its habit of scratching the ground with its feet to find food.

022.Chuck_will_Widow.habitat: Open woodlands, forest edges, and agricultural areas in the southeastern United States.
022.Chuck_will_Widow.range_description: Found in the southeastern United States, from Texas to Florida, and parts of southern Georgia and South Carolina.
022.Chuck_will_Widow.migration: Non-migratory; remains in its range year-round.
field_marks: Dark brown to black plumage with a distinctive white eye ring.
Short, broad wings with a pale edge visible in flight.
Long, slender tail with a white tip.
Bill is short and slightly hooked, with a pale base.
022.Chuck_will_Widow.diet: Insects, especially moths, beetles, and other flying invertebrates.

similar_species.name: Common nighthawk
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Chuck-will's-widow has a more uniform dark coloration and a white eye ring, whereas the Common nighthawk has a more mottled appearance and lacks the eye ring.

similar_species.name: Eastern screech-owl
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Chuck-will's-widow is a bird, not an owl, and has a more elongated body with a distinct white tail tip, while the Eastern screech-owl has a rounder body and lacks the tail pattern.

022.Chuck_will_Widow.fun_fact: Chuck-will's-widow is known for its distinctive, eerie call that sounds like a 'chuck-will-de-widow' and is often heard at dusk.

023.Brandt_Cormorant.habitat: Coastal marine environments, including rocky shores and estuaries, with access to open water for fishing.
023.Brandt_Cormorant.range_description: Breeds in coastal regions of the North Pacific, including Alaska, British Columbia, and the Aleutian Islands. Non-breeding individuals may range further south along the Pacific coast.
023.Brandt_Cormorant.migration: Non-migratory; remains in coastal habitats year-round.
field_marks: Black body with a distinctive white patch on the neck and upper breast.
Long, narrow, hooked bill with a yellowish tip.
Dark eyes with a pale ring around the eye.
Long, slender tail with a slight fork.
Wings are long and pointed, with a dark upper surface and pale underparts.
023.Brandt_Cormorant.diet: Primarily fish, which it catches by diving from the surface. Also consumes crustaceans and insects.

similar_species.name: Great Cormorant
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Great Cormorant has a more robust build, a larger bill, and lacks the distinct white neck patch present in Brandt Cormorant.

similar_species.name: Pelagic Cormorant
similar_species.how_to_distinguish: Pelagic Cormorant has a more streamlined body, a shorter and less hooked bill, and lacks the white neck patch of Brandt Cormorant.

100.Brown_Pelican.habitat: Coastal marine environments, estuaries, and shallow bays, primarily in tropical and subtropical regions.
